topicName: Sprint Planning: Goal Setting and Capacity Planning
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Sprint Planning: Goal Setting and Capacity Planning in Scrum"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sprint Planning is a critical Scrum event where the entire Scrum Team collaborates to define the work of the upcoming Sprint. The resulting plan is created by the collaborative work of the entire Scrum Team. This tutorial covers the foundational mechanics of effective goal setting and accurate capacity planning."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Part 1: The Anatomy of a Sprint Goal"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Sprint Goal is a single objective for the Sprint, agreed upon by the Product Owner and the Developers. It provides guidance to the Development Team on why it is building the Increment. It is created during the Sprint Planning event."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Purpose: Aligns the team on a unified business or technical objective rather than a disjointed list of tickets."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Flexibility: Provides flexibility regarding the exact work needed in the Product Backlog to achieve it."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Commitment: Fosters team commitment and shared accountability."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Part 2: Calculating Team Capacity"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Capacity planning ensures that the team does not overcommit. Capacity is measured in hours or days, distinct from velocity which is measured in story points. Accurate capacity planning factors in holidays, PTO, company meetings, and support overhead."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Total Team Capacity = Sum of (Developer Working Days * Hours per Day * Focus Factor)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'Focus Factor' (typically between 0.60 to 0.80) accounts for non-project activities like emails, impromptu meetings, and administrative overhead. For example, a team of 5 developers working for 10 days with a focus factor of 0.70 has a capacity of 280 hours."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Part 3: Pulling Items into the Sprint Backlog"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the capacity is known, Developers pull items from the top of the Product Backlog. They select items that they believe they can complete while aiming to fulfill the Sprint Goal. Each selected item should be broken down into tasks estimated in hours."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check total estimated task hours against the calculated team capacity."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure the Definition of Done (DoD) can be met for every selected Product Backlog Item."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stop pulling work when capacity is reached, even if there is remaining team velocity from past sprints."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Effective Sprint Planning relies on a clear, inspiring Sprint Goal combined with realistic capacity calculations. By preventing overcommitment, Scrum Teams ensure sustainable delivery paces and high-quality increments at every Sprint Review."}]
